speed.comparisons_note: Andrey 0.9.0 against Tetrad on the same datasets, on the same node in one job. A dataset's time is its timed fit; seconds_ref and seconds_090 are medians over the size's datasets, and speedup is seconds_ref / seconds_090. errors_ref and errors_090 are each side's median shd against the true graph's CPDAG (the PAG of the observed variables for FCI) over the row's 5 datasets. same_graph_datasets counts the datasets on which both packages returned the same graph. seconds_ref is the search inside the JVM (JVM start, source compile, and data loading excluded, as Andrey's time excludes interpreter start and imports) and process_s_ref is the whole call. note states what was measured about the difference between the two packages' errors. matched repeats the comparison over every dataset a diagnosis run covered (20 at d = 20 to 100 and 10 at d = 200; 30 for PC at d = 50), as the mean of each dataset's errors, Andrey's over its seeds; difference is Andrey minus Tetrad, difference_95 its percentile bootstrap 95% interval over the datasets (4,000 resamples). The first entry uses the row's settings; each later entry changes the one setting it names. The GES entries ran Andrey's serial search, which returns the same graph as the parallel one. A median over 5 datasets is fragile for a search that makes one start; the means are the stable figures.

boundary.disclaimer: For reference, measured on the data generators named in each ladder with the settings listed per ladder; not a hard limit.
boundary.note: A ladder steps one quantity on one regime until a stop; its axis is 'd' (variables; hidden and latent nodes count where a regime has them), 'n' (rows: the pair methods, whose d is 2) or 'latents' (gin: a rung's d counts each latent variable and its 3 indicators, 4 per latent, and 3 per latent are observed), and its label describes the regime in plain words (tau is the lag window of a time-series method). A rung is through when fewer than 3 of its fits did not finish within the caps (a timeout, an out-of-memory kill, or an error); median_errors is over the finished fits and null when none finished, so a fit that did not finish never counts as an empty graph. beats_empty compares the median errors with the empty graph's. median_time_s is null on a rung whose fits ran on two CPU models (cpu names both). A regime 'degK-nN' has mean degree K and N rows at every d; 'degK-nMd' has M x d rows. A ladder ends with stop 'time', 'memory' or 'error' (3 fits of a rung did not finish), 'accuracy' (two rungs in a row did not beat the empty graph), or 'ladder_end' (the last planned rung); end.hand_stopped marks an accuracy stop set by hand after larger rungs had run, and those rungs stay. beats_empty_through_d is the largest d up to which every rung is through and beats the empty graph; last_through_d and first_not_beating_d are on the same axis, and a ladder with axis 'n' carries all three as *_n (rows) with the *_d fields null. params holds the keyword arguments of the public andrey.<method>(data, **params) call whose values differ from its defaults ({} when all are defaults), and params_note says where a setting's meaning on this release differs from the build that ran it; generators gives the call that draws each dataset of a rung, with the rung's d, n, mean degree and seed.
